newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Gov says income tax cut might total $234 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Gov says income tax cut might total $234 mln.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, who in August announced a tax cut, on Friday said the total amount could grow to $234 million if the legislature agreed to return the funds to taxpayers.
If the governor's proposal were approved, the personal exemptions for single filers would rise to about $5,155 from $3,400, while joint filers would see an increase to $6,670 from $4,400.

And for individual filers, the personal exemption would climb to $3,335 from $2,200. A spokesman for the governor was not immediately available to explain how Massachusetts defines its different categories of filers.
"For too long, government has been trying to find excuses to spend people's money," said Weld, in prepared remarks.
Under a 10-year old law, surplus state funds have to be deposited in a Rainy Day or stabilization fund, but when it reaches $543 million, any extra funds must be returned to the taxpayers.
The surplus totaled $150 million in August, and now has climbed by another $84 million, Weld said.
If the legislature approves the bigger tax cut, it would be worth about $135 for married couples, $105 for heads of households, and $67 for single filers.
